feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — A metadata tag is a conceptual label, not a physical object.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — It is a human-created structure designed to categorize and annotate.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not inspired by biological processes.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Tags do not require or involve power or energy to exist as concepts.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — They provide structure symbolically, not physically.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Representations are visible; the tag itself is a symbolic abstraction.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Exists as a symbolic layer in data models, independent of any specific medium.
feedback.Active: Excluded — It does not act, only describes or encodes.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Excluded — A tag is a representational structure, not a functional artifact or tool.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Tags influence processing but produce no output themselves.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Tags are the data to be processed, they do not process anything themselves.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Tags annotate states; they do not change them directly.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Interpreted by users, but not an interactive construct itself.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Used by systems, but not themselves embedded functionality.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Tags require interpretation; they do not function on their own.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Many systems function without tagging; it is an organizational layer.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Conveys attributes, categories, and relationships to systems or users.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Tag schemas and formats follow explicit conventions and rules.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Tags may be nested, compound, or structured in sets.
feedback.Normative: Excluded — Tags follow standards, but do not impose behavior or expectation themselves.
feedback.Meta: Included — It is the quintessential example of meta-data (data about data).
feedback.Temporal: Excluded — Tags are typically static labels, even if they represent time (e.g., a timestamp).
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Exists entirely in digital or conceptual form.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Tagging vocabularies and their meanings are defined by communities or platforms.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Standardized formats (e.g., Dublin Core, schema.org) are institutionally maintained.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Tags may encode identifiers, but identity linkage is contextual, not intrinsic.
feedback.Regulated: Excluded — Tagging standards may be adopted, but tags are not governed by law.
feedback.Economically Significant: Excluded — It enables economic activity, but is not itself an economic entity.
feedback.Politicised: Excluded — The use of tags may be political, but the tag itself is not.
feedback.Ritualised: Excluded — Not part of symbolic or ceremonial practice.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Excluded — Tags may contribute to ethical concerns (e.g., bias), but are not inherently ethical units.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats metadata tags as synthetic, symbolic, and rule-governed abstractions used to annotate other data. Their function is performed through interpretation by external systems, not by the tag itself. Social traits reflect their origin in group-defined labeling standards, but exclude role or behavior traits not intrinsic to tagging structure.
